Consider the picture above. Given that $c=a+\lambda b,$ find $\lambda .$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find $\lambda ,$ we want to match the expression

$$
c=a+\lambda b.
$$

We are given that one of the components is $a.$ So, we begin with the vector $a,$ and then find the remaining vector needed to reach the point $C.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186096701/plots/0a275b02eca749f5d1deaac2c100dc394f84626d37e176507102e325a55529a9.png)

Note that in $△OAC,$ we have:

- $AC=\frac{7}{3}|b|$

- $\overset{\to }{AC}$ and $b$ have the same direction

Hence, $\overset{\to }{AC}=\frac{7}{3}b.$

Additionally,

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =\overset{\to }{OA}+\overset{\to }{AC} \\  & =a+\frac{7}{3}b.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $c=a+\lambda b=a+\frac{7}{3}b.$

Since $a∦b,$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients of $b,$ we get:

$$
\lambda =\frac{7}{3}
$$

$$

Consequently, $c=\lambda a+3b=\frac{5}{2}a+3b.$

Consider the picture above. Given that $c=\lambda a+\frac{5}{3}b$, find $\lambda .$

The grid has unit squares. The exact point coordinates are $O=(0,0)$, $A=(2, 0)$, $B=(-2, -1)$, and $C=(\frac{1}{6}, - \frac{5}{3})$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find $\lambda ,$ we want to match the expression

$$
c=\lambda a+\frac{5}{3}b.
$$

We are given that one of the components is $\frac{5}{3}b.$ So, we first draw the vector $\frac{5}{3}b$ from the origin. Then we complete the path to the point $C.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186096701/plots/ba71c5cf69a49df939393408fbf766f147b3cfb6ac796501bdc5b4138730dc0d.png)

Let $P$ be the endpoint of the vector $\frac{5}{3}b.$ Then

$$
c=\overset{\to }{OP}+\overset{\to }{PC}.
$$

The endpoint of the known component has coordinates

$$
P=(- \frac{10}{3}, - \frac{5}{3}).
$$

The remaining horizontal displacement is

$$
\frac{1}{6}-(- \frac{10}{3})=\frac{7}{2}.
$$

Compared with the horizontal length of $a$, its scalar factor is

$$
\frac{\frac{7}{2}}{2}=\frac{7}{4}.
$$

In $△OPC,$ we have:

- $PC=\frac{7}{4}|a|$

- $\overset{\to }{PC}$ and $a$ have the same direction

Hence, $\overset{\to }{PC}=\frac{7}{4}a.$

Additionally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =\overset{\to }{OP}+\overset{\to }{PC} \\  & =\frac{5}{3}b+\frac{7}{4}a.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $c=\lambda a+\frac{5}{3}b=\frac{7}{4}a+\frac{5}{3}b.$

Since $a∦b,$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients of $a,$ we get:

$$
\lambda =\frac{7}{4}
$$
